definitions.explanation: Having an iron face — utterly shameless and impervious to embarrassment or criticism. Describes someone who acts shamelessly without any sign of remorse or self-consciousness. Always negative in nuance.

examples.japanese: あの{男|おとこ}は{鉄面皮|てつめんぴ}だ。
{嘘|うそ}がばれても{平気|へいき}でいるとは、{鉄面皮|てつめんぴ}にも{程|ほど}がある。
examples.english: Remaining calm even after being caught in a lie — there are limits to being shameless.

examples.japanese: {自分|じぶん}の{失敗|しっぱい}を{認|みと}めず、{鉄面皮|てつめんぴ}な{態度|たいど}で{押|お}し{通|とお}した。
examples.english: Without admitting his own mistake, he pushed through with a brazen attitude.

notes:
USAGE:
Literally means "iron face skin." Used as both a な-adjective ({鉄面皮|てつめんぴ}な{態度|たいど}) and a noun ({鉄面皮|てつめんぴ}だ). The word is always critical — it describes someone who should feel shame but does not.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鉄面皮|てつめんぴ}な{態度|たいど} (brazen attitude)
- {鉄面皮|てつめんぴ}な{人|ひと} (shameless person)
- {鉄面皮|てつめんぴ}にも{程|ほど}がある (there are limits to being shameless)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{厚|あつ}かましい (impudent) and {図|ず}々しい (brazen, pushy) are more colloquial alternatives. {鉄面皮|てつめんぴ} is more literary and emphatic.
